rows.search: Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 27 = ס״ח תש״ס 1750 p. 261 (8.8.2000) per the Hebrew Wikisource header of חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (he.wikisource.org, action=raw, line 5 maps every ס״ח page to an amendment number) and WIPO Lex IL104 (wipo.int/wipolex/en/text/385541, Nevo's annotated consolidated text): it replaced s. 13 (opening of the Knesset), s. 20(a) (until a Speaker is elected the senior MK, 'ותיק', presides instead of the eldest; the PM, PM-elect, ministers and deputy ministers excluded) and s. 20A(b) (acting Speaker during incapacity). (1) Hayut's survey in HCJ 5658/23, Versa node/705 read in four passes (offsets 0, 100000, 200000, 300000): the only Basic-Law petitions listed are Bergman-line election cases, Bar-On 4908/10, Academic Center 8260/16, Shafir 5969/20, Rotation Government 2905/20, Scheinfeld, Hasson 5555/18, Shapira 4076/20, Ben Meir 5744/16, Quintinsky 10042/16; none concerns this amendment. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת (raw wikitext, grep תיקון/בג״ץ/עתיר): the amendments list covers Nos. 9, 10, 12, 30, 35, 42, 44, 49, 50, 51 only; the only petition it names is HCJ 5969/20 against Amendment 50. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): עתירה בג״ץ "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 27)" OR "תיקון מס' 27" "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת" 2000 יושב ראש הכנסת בפועל פתיחת הכנסת → only the Knesset PDF (fs.knesset.gov.il/15/law/15_lsr_300247.pdf, geo-blocked) and an IDI Parliament piece describing the change; no petition.
rows.note: Procedural amendment on who presides at the opening sitting; no petition traced in any source consulted.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Basic Law: The Government (1992) Amendment No. 10 = ס״ח תשס״א 48 (19.12.2000) per the 'חוק קודם' header of the Wikisource text of חוק-יסוד: הממשלה (Knesset PDF 15_lsr_300283.pdf, geo-blocked). Content from press: the 'Netanyahu law' allowing a citizen who is not an MK to stand in the special election for Prime Minister after Barak's resignation (first reading 63-46-1; Walla 19.12.2000, news.walla.co.il/item/34041 and /34000, headline 'חוק נתניהו התקבל למרות התנגדותו של האיש על שמו הוא קרוי'). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705, all four passes: no case on the 1992 Government law. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הממשלה (1992) (raw, grep תיקון/2000/בחירות מיוחדות/בג״ץ/עתיר): says only that the 1992 law was amended ten times; no petition; and הבחירות המיוחדות לראשות הממשלה – 2001 (grep חוק/פיזור/בג״ץ/עתיר): describes the dissolution bills and Netanyahu's conditional candidacy, no petition. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס' 10)" התשס"א 2000 ... בחירות מיוחדות; "חוק נתניהו" דצמבר 2000 הכנסת אישרה תיקון חוק יסוד הממשלה מועמד שאינו חבר כנסת; עתירה לבג"ץ נגד "חוק נתניהו" 2000 ...; English: Netanyahu December 2000 Knesset amendment non-member candidate special election petition High Court → no petition found (results concern 2019-2023 petitions about Netanyahu forming a government).
rows.related_cases: None found. The amendment was never used (Netanyahu did not run; Sharon beat Barak on 6.2.2001) and the 1992 law was replaced on 7.3.2001.
rows.note: Content of the amendment rests on press reports, not the text (Knesset PDF geo-blocked); reviewer should confirm from ס״ח 1762.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 31 = ס״ח תשס״א 1796 p. 426 (24.6.2001) per the Wikisource header; Wikisource section tag תשס״א־4 and WIPO Lex IL104 note: it repealed s. 32 (if the Knesset had not convened within the four weeks of s. 31 it would meet on the Monday of the fifth week at 4 p.m.). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705, four passes: nothing. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת: amendment not listed, no petition. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 31)" OR "תיקון מס' 31" "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת" 2001 ביטול סעיף 32 כינוס הכנסת עתירה בג"ץ → only neighbouring amendments (8, 25, 37) and WIPO text; no petition.
rows.note: Housekeeping repeal of an obsolete convening rule.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Basic Law: The President (Amendment No. 6) = ס״ח תשס״ב 1809 p. 2 (30.10.2001); Nevo/WIPO Lex IL108 (wipo.int/wipolex/en/text/385543) number it 5 '[במקור מס' 6]' because a 2003 act also bears No. 6. It amended President s. 11(a)(2) (functions under Basic Law: The Government, re dissolution of the Knesset and resignation of the PM) and s. 12 (countersignature by the PM or another minister designated by the government; documents on forming a government or dissolving the Knesset excepted), and, counted as Knesset Amendment No. 34 (Wikisource header תשס״ב 2; tag תשס״ב on s. 20), added 'ראש הממשלה הנבחר' to s. 20(a); in force 28.1.2003, election day of the 16th Knesset, as a consequential of Basic Law: The Government (2001). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing on the President law. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: נשיא המדינה (WebFetch): no amendments table; petitions cited (HCJ 428/86 Barzilai, 6163/92 Eisenberg, 2678/07 Katsav, 219/09) concern application of the law, none an amendment. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: נשיא המדינה (תיקון מס' 6)" 2001 ... יושב ראש הכנסת ממלא מקום הנשיא; עתירה בג"ץ "חוק-יסוד: נשיא המדינה (תיקון מס' 5)" OR "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 34)" 2001 "ראש הממשלה הנבחר" חתימת קיום פיזור הכנסת → no petition (results concern the 2023 incapacity amendment HCJ 2412/23).
rows.note: Numbering discrepancy (Nevo: No. 5) should be recorded against the sheet's 'No. 6'.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Basic Law: The Judiciary (Amendment No. 2) = ס״ח תשס״ב 1864 p. 598 (5.8.2002): s. 7(4) amended to add the Ombudsman for Complaints against Judges to those who may propose ending a judge's tenure (Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: השפיטה via WebFetch; Wikisource tag תשס״ב on s. 7). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: the only Judiciary-law challenge is HCJ 5658/23 against Amendment No. 3. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: השפיטה: lists amendments 1992, 2002, 2023, 2025; petitions mentioned only HCJ 5658/23; none against Amendment 2. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): עתירה בג"ץ "נציב תלונות הציבור על שופטים" חוק יסוד: השפיטה תיקון 2002 סעיף 7 ...; "חוק-יסוד: השפיטה (תיקון מס' 2)" OR "תיקון מס' 2 לחוק-יסוד: השפיטה" 2002 ... עתירה בג"ץ → only 2024-2025 petitions (Lavi on the vacant post; Movement for Quality Government and Israel Bar against the 2025 ordinary law changing how the Ombudsman is chosen), none against the 2002 amendment.
rows.related_cases: 2024-2025 petitions concerning the Ombudsman's appointment (Lavi v. Fogelman and Levin; Movement for Quality Government and Israel Bar against the 2025 selection law) attack ordinary law or administrative conduct, not this amendment; case numbers not verified.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 36 = ס״ח תשס״ד 1933 p. 336 (30.3.2004); Wikisource tag תשס״ד on s. 6A and WIPO Lex IL104: a consequential change to s. 6A(a) so that the conditions for a recognised faction split refer to 'the law' (Knesset Law 1994, s. 59) rather than the Knesset Elections Law. (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת: amendment not listed, no petition. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 36)" OR "חוק יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 36)" 2004 פרישה מסיעה סעיף 6א → Knesset PDF 16_lsr_300994.pdf, 2022 Knesset legal adviser's response in the Chikli matter, Knesset research note; no petition. Follow-up WebSearch שקלי "סעיף 6א" "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת" בג"ץ 2022 ... → no case number found.
rows.related_cases: The 2022 Chikli matter (s. 6A applied by the Knesset House Committee and the Central Elections Committee for the 25th Knesset to MK Amichai Chikli's candidacy on the Likud list; Knesset legal adviser's response static.zman.co.il/www/uploads/2022/09/...) applied s. 6A; the High Court docket number was not located.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 38 = ס״ח תשס״ז 2090 p. 158 (28.3.2007); Wikisource tag תשס״ז on s. 42B and WIPO Lex IL104: s. 42B replaced so that an MK convicted of an offence that the court determines involves moral turpitude is suspended automatically from that determination until the judgment is final, and an MK sentenced to imprisonment for the term served; the former discretionary suspension by the Knesset Committee (old (c)) repealed. (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת: not listed; no petition. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 38)" ... 2007 השעיה חבר הכנסת שהורשע; "סעיף 42ב" "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת" השעיה ... בג"ץ עתירה "תיקון מס' 38" 2007 → Constitution Committee protocol of 20.3.2007 on the bill (Erdan/Yachimovich), IDI Parliament note on s. 42A-42B, HCJ 10214/16 (which concerns the 2016 expulsion law, Amendment 44); no petition against Amendment 38.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 10214/16 (ACRI/Adalah, expulsion law, Amendment No. 44, dismissed 27.5.2018) concerns a different amendment of the same chapter.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Amendment No. 2 of 2013 = ס״ח תשע״ג 52 (20.3.2013), listed in the Wikisource header of חוק-יסוד: משק המדינה as 'תיקון מס' 2 לחוק-יסוד: תקציב המדינה לשנים 2009 עד 2012 (הוראות מיוחדות) (הוראת שעה)', followed by Amendment No. 3 (ס״ח תשע״ג 70, title 'לשנים 2009 עד 2012 ולשנת 2013') and Amendment No. 4 (ס״ח תשע״ה 194, 'לשנים 2009 עד 2014'). (1) Hayut survey, HCJ 5658/23 paras 53-59 (Versa node/705, offset 100000): the budget temporary provisions were challenged only in Bar-On HCJ 4908/10 (the 2010 amendment setting a 2011-2012 budget; dismissed, with a warning against temporary provisions) and Academic Center HCJ 8260/16 (the 2017-2018 law, called the fifth repetition; nullification notice); no 2013 petition mentioned. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: משק המדינה (section תיקון החוק בהוראות שעה) and תקציב המדינה (ישראל) (section תקציב דו-שנתי): mention only HCJ 4908/10 and HCJ 8260/16. (3) Versa Bar-On page (versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/bar-v-knesset): 2010 amendment only; no Versa translation of 8260/16 located (site search returned nothing). (4) WebSearch (Hebrew): עתירה בג"ץ 2013 חוק-יסוד: תקציב המדינה לשנים 2009 עד 2012 ולשנת 2013 הוראת שעה תקציב דו-שנתי 2013-2014 התנועה למען איכות השלטון; "8260/16" ... 2013 2015 ... "הפעם החמישית"; idi.org.il-restricted search תקציב דו-שנתי הוראת שעה חוק יסוד 2013 2015 2017 בג"ץ ...; English search on 8260/16 and the 2013/2015 extensions → nothing on a 2013 petition.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 4908/10 Bar-On v. Knesset (judgment 7.4.2011; dismissed; Beinisch: the Knesset should refrain from amending constitutional provisions by temporary provision) attacked the 2010 amendment; HCJ 8260/16 Academic Center of Law and Business v. Knesset (judgment 6.9.2017; petition dismissed with an invalidity warning that a non-annual budget may no longer be set by temporary provision) attacked Basic Law: State Budget for 2017 and 2018 (Special Provisions)(Temporary Provision). Neither attacked the 2013 amendments.
rows.note: Absence of a 2013 petition is inferred from Hayut's survey and the secondary sources; the Academic Center judgment itself (which recounts the extensions) was not read.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Basic Law: The President (Amendment No. 9) = ס״ח תשע״ד 2411 p. 32 (7.11.2013); Nevo/WIPO Lex IL108 note: amended s. 8(a) (election of the President by majority; Hebrew Wikipedia: if no candidate wins a majority, the two leading candidates go to a further round in which a plurality suffices; first applied in the 2014 election); Wikisource tag תשע״ד on s. 8. (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: נשיא המדינה: no petition against any amendment. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: נשיא המדינה (תיקון מס' 9)" OR "תיקון מס' 9" "נשיא המדינה" 2013 סיבוב שני בחירת הנשיא עתירה בג"ץ → Constitution Committee protocol (July 2013, unanimous approval) and Knesset research note; no petition.

Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 41 = ס״ח תשע״ד 2452 p. 554 (22.5.2014); the Wikisource headers of the Government (2001) and President laws also list it (tag תשע״ד־2 on Knesset s. 41, Government s. 22, President s. 19); WIPO Lex IL104/IL108: resignation of an MK, minister or President takes effect 48 hours after the letter reaches the Speaker unless withdrawn, and a period ending on a rest day is deferred to the next working day (the rest-day rule is the new element; the 48-hour rule predates it). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת and חוק יסוד: הממשלה: not listed as contested. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): עתירה בג"ץ "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 41)" OR "תיקון מס' 41" "חוק-יסוד: הכנסת" 2014 התפטרות חבר הכנסת 48 שעות חזרה מהתפטרות → Knesset bill memorandum 19_ls1_271718, law text 19_lsr_303801, Maariv opinion on the Edelstein case; no petition.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 2144/20 Movement for Quality Government v. Speaker of the Knesset (23.3.2020, Edelstein) concerned the Speaker's duty to convene the plenum; Edelstein's resignation then ran under s. 41's 48-hour rule. Not a challenge to this amendment; citation from memory, verify.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Knesset Amendment No. 42 and Temporary Provision = ס״ח תשע״ה 2500 p. 248 (6.8.2015; passed 30.7.2015, 64-51), the 'small Norwegian law': for the 20th Knesset only, added s. 42C (a minister or deputy minister may end Knesset membership and be replaced by the next candidate on the list, returning on leaving office; one per list), amended ss. 23 and 43, and amended Basic Law: The Government (s. 4 of the act; Government Wikisource header תשע״ה 249). (1) Hayut survey, HCJ 5658/23: para 112 (Versa node/705, offset 100000, re-read) cites 'HCJ 4076/20 Shapira v. Knesset' only for the description of the Norwegian-law mechanism (replacement MKs may feel beholden to the government); it does not say what that petition attacked or its outcome. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הכנסת (Amendment 42 entry: no petition), חוק יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס' 49) (raw, grep בג״ץ/עתיר/4076/2015: describes 2015 and 2020 versions, no petition), החוק הנורווגי הקטן (redirect). (3) WebSearch: "החוק הנורבגי" 2015 עתירה לבג"ץ נגד החוק "תיקון מס' 42" ...; English "Norwegian law" Israel 2015 petition "High Court" ...; three searches for "4076/20" (Hebrew and English, with שפירא/הנורווגי/42ג) → the 2020 case could not be located; no 2015 petition found.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 4076/20 Shapira v. Knesset, cited in HCJ 5658/23 para 112 as describing s. 42C; by its 2020 docket year it concerns the permanent expanded law (Amendment No. 49, 16.6.2020) rather than this temporary provision, which lapsed with the 20th Knesset; its target and outcome were not verified.
rows.note: Reviewer should pull HCJ 4076/20 from Nevo or supremedecisions to confirm it attacked Amendment 49 and not the 2015 act.

rows.search: Enactment identified: State Economy Amendment No. 9 = ס״ח תשע״ז 2587 p. 32 (12.12.2016); Wikisource tag תשע״ז on s. 3; IDI's table of Basic-Law changes (idi.org.il/articles/33479) describes it as 'procedural matters and defense budget' (consistent with s. 3(b)(3), the detailed defence budget laid before the joint Finance/Foreign Affairs and Defence committee); the Knesset PDF 20_lsr_364293.pdf is geo-blocked, so the exact text was not read. (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: HCJ 8260/16 concerned the separate 2017-2018 budget Basic Law (ס״ח תשע״ו 1182, August 2016), not Amendment 9. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: משק המדינה: does not mention Amendment 9. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): "חוק-יסוד: משק המדינה (תיקון מס' 9)" 2016; "תיקון מס' 9" "חוק-יסוד: משק המדינה" ... דצמבר 2016 ...; "משק המדינה" "תיקון מס' 9" 2016 "תקציב הביטחון" OR "ועדה משותפת" ... עתירה בג"ץ → no petition.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 8260/16 Academic Center v. Knesset (6.9.2017) attacked the contemporaneous Basic Law: State Budget for 2017 and 2018 (Special Provisions)(Temporary Provision), not this amendment.
rows.note: Content description rests on IDI's one-line summary; verify against ס״ח 2587.

rows.search: Enactment identified: Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 5) = ס״ח תשע״ח 2682 p. 112 (14.1.2018), the 'Litzman law': s. 33 amended so that a Prime Minister who holds a ministry may delegate the minister's powers to a deputy minister in that ministry (Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הממשלה; Wikisource tag תשע״ח on s. 33; IDI table 'passed within two days'). (1) Hayut survey, Versa node/705: nothing on this amendment. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הממשלה (WebFetch and raw grep): describes the amendment; names no petition against it; cites HCJ 3132/15. (3) WebSearch (Hebrew): ליצמן סגן שר הבריאות עתירה בג"ץ 2018 תיקון חוק-יסוד: הממשלה אצילת סמכויות ...; עתירה לבג"ץ נגד "חוק ליצמן" 2018 ... → only the 2015 judgment and reports of the bill as a 'bypass' of it; no petition against the amendment.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 3132/15 Yesh Atid v. Prime Minister (23.8.2015): held that 'deputy minister with the status of minister' has no legal validity; the amendment was enacted to allow Litzman's return as deputy health minister.

rows.search: Enactment identified: State Economy (Amendment No. 10 and Temporary Provision for 2020) = ס״ח תש״ף 2791 pp. 16-18 (7.4.2020); Wikisource tag תש״ף on s. 3B; Hebrew Wikipedia and Calcalist: enacted at the Attorney General's demand to put coronavirus spending into primary legislation; it let the government exceed the continuing budget (one twelfth of the 2019 budget per month) for coronavirus needs in declining monthly caps (2.65% of the 2019 budget in April falling to 0.35% in December). (1) Hayut survey, HCJ 5658/23 paras 58-59: Shafir attacked Amendment No. 50 to Basic Law: The Knesset (temporary provision), which 'indirectly amended Basic Law: The State Economy to raise the 2020 continuation-budget ceiling by 11 billion shekels'; the Rotation Government case (HCJ 2905/20) concerned the May 2020 regime amendments. (2) Hebrew Wikipedia התראת בטלות (raw, grep 5969/שפיר/משק המדינה): the petition sought annulment of Amendment 50 to Basic Law: The Knesset; the invalidity warning says the State Economy law may not be amended to raise the continuing-budget ceiling for purposes foreign to the mechanism. (3) Calcalist 2.9.2020 (calcalist.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-3847703,00.html): the אחריות לאומית petition (adv. Gilad Barnea; Justice Mintz ordered responses by 16.9.2020) asked to void s. 2 of Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 50 – Temporary Provision), i.e. the 11-billion addition; Walla 23.5.2021 (walla.co.il/news/politics/3437311): judgment 6-3, invalidity warning. (4) IDI (idi.org.il/articles/33588, Feb 2021): petitions pending against the August 2020 Knesset amendment and the alternate-government amendment; none against the State Economy 'budget boxes'. (5) WebSearch (Hebrew): "תיקון מס' 10 והוראת שעה לשנת 2020" חוק-יסוד: משק המדינה עתירה בג"ץ קופסאות קורונה תקציב המשכי; "קופסאות קורונה" עתירה בג"ץ 2020 ... → only the Amendment-50 petition.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 5969/20 Shafir v. Knesset (judgment 23.5.2021; invalidity warning, 6-3) attacked Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 50 – Temporary Provision) of 24.8.2020, whose s. 2 amended the 2020 temporary provision created by this act (the Wikisource header lists that indirect amendment at ס״ח תש״ף 420 between (תיקון מס' 3) and (תיקון מס' 5)); HCJ 2905/20 Movement for Quality Government v. Knesset (judgment 12.7.2021) attacked Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 8 and Temporary Provision).
rows.note: Coded no challenge because the petitions attacked Amendment 50 (a later enactment) rather than this act; a reviewer who treats an attack on the later amendment of the temporary provision as an attack on the provision should re-code. Whether HCJ 2905/20 also named the May 2020 '(תיקון)' to this act (ס״ח תש״ף 46) was not checked.

rows.search: Enactment identified: (Amendment No. 2) to the 2020 temporary provision = ס״ח תש״ף 2828 p. 230 (16.7.2020); Wikisource tag תש״ף־3 on s. 3B; ynet economy (ynet.co.il/economy/article/HJg11ST2kD) and Arutz 7 14.7.2020 (inn.co.il/news/443557, first reading): raised the 2020 continuing-budget ceiling by about NIS 25 billion earmarked for the coronavirus economic-aid plan (about 7.7 billion to the National Insurance Institute, 15.7 billion in grants to businesses and the self-employed, 1.3 billion arnona relief), on top of about 50 billion added in April and June; passed 67-0 with three abstentions. IDI's table lists it as 'budget boxes', July 2020. Searches as for seq 101 (Hayut paras 58-59; Hebrew Wikipedia התראת בטלות; Calcalist 2.9.2020; Walla 23.5.2021; IDI 33588; WebSearch "קופסאות קורונה" עתירה בג"ץ 2020 ...; "תיקון מס' 10 והוראת שעה לשנת 2020" ... עתירה) → no petition against this amendment; the only 2020 budget petitions attacked Amendment 50 to Basic Law: The Knesset.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 5969/20 Shafir v. Knesset (23.5.2021) concerned Amendment 50 to Basic Law: The Knesset and its indirect 11-billion addition, not this amendment.

rows.search: Enactment identified: (Amendment No. 6) to the 2020 temporary provision = ס״ח תשפ״א 2858 p. 28 (30.9.2020); Wikisource tag תשפ״א on s. 3B (sub-sections (a)(1)(e), (a1), (a2) now marked 'פקע'). Content not verified: the Knesset PDF 23_lsr_584149.pdf is geo-blocked; a Knesset Finance Committee document (main.knesset.gov.il/Activity/committees/Finance/Documents/csafim20-2.pdf, text garbled) records further amendments of the temporary provision in June, July and September 2020, one of 7.9.2020 with a programme of about NIS 6.7 billion, which may be Amendment No. 5 (ס״ח תש״ף 436) rather than No. 6; IDI's table lists a second 'budget boxes' amendment in September 2020. deviations: Knesset sites are geo-blocked as the sheet warns (fs.knesset.gov.il answers HTTP 303 to a block page), and web.archive.org could not be fetched from this environment (the fetch tool refuses it), so no amendment was read from its official text. Contents were taken instead from WIPO Lex's copies of Nevo's annotated consolidated texts (IL104 Knesset, IL108 President), the Hebrew Wikisource section tags and headers, Hebrew Wikipedia, IDI's table of Basic-Law changes, and press; rows 61, 94 and 109 rest on thin descriptions and should be checked against ספר החוקים.

Versa has no translation I could find of HCJ 5969/20 Shafir, HCJ 8260/16 Academic Center, HCJ 2905/20 or HCJ 4076/20 (its site search returned 'no results' for Shafir and Academic Center). What the 2020 petitions attacked is therefore taken from Hayut's survey in HCJ 5658/23 (Versa node/705, paras 53-59 and 112), Hebrew Wikipedia התראת בטלות, Calcalist 2.9.2020 and Walla 23.5.2021, all of which name only Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 50 – Temporary Provision) and its s. 2 indirect amendment; the Shafir judgment itself was not read, so a reviewer should confirm from it that no consolidated petition also named the April, July or September 2020 State Economy acts.

HCJ 4076/20 Shapira v. Knesset (cited at para 112 of HCJ 5658/23 for the Norwegian law) could not be located in three searches; its coding as not a challenge to seq 89 rests only on its 2020 docket year and the lapse of the 2015 temporary provision with the 20th Knesset.

Nevo's case-law search, supremedecisions.court.gov.il and the petitioners' own case lists (mqg.org.il, acri.org.il, adalah.org, idi.org.il case pages) were not searched directly, only through general web searches (one search restricted to idi.org.il); the tool budget was spent on identifying the content of eighteen mostly obscure amendments.

Hayut's survey (Versa node/705) was read through the fetch tool's summaries in four 100,000-character passes, not verbatim; the summaries report that no Basic-Law petition other than those listed appears, but a direct read is advisable for paras 50-68.

Related-case details given from memory and flagged as such: HCJ 2144/20 (Edelstein, 23.3.2020), the 12.7.2021 date of HCJ 2905/20, the 27.5.2018 dismissal of HCJ 10214/16, and the Chikli 2022 matter (no docket number found).

Numbering notes for the reviewer: the 2001 President amendment the sheet calls No. 6 is No. 5 in Nevo's numbering ('במקור מס' 6'); the same act is counted as Knesset Amendment No. 34; the 2015 Norwegian-law act also carries Government-law provisions (ס״ח תשע״ה 249); Amendment 41 of 2014 also amended the Government and President laws.
The 2013 row (seq 80) is coded on the absence of any 2013 petition in Hayut's survey, Hebrew Wikipedia and searches; the Academic Center judgment, which recounts the extensions, was not read.
